Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: Not, Watching, When

outputs.L1:
Not every man knows what he shall sing at the end,  
watching the pier as the ship sails away, or what it will be like  
when he is held motionless by the sea’s roar, there at the end,  
or what he shall hope for once it becomes clear that he will never return.

When the time for pruning the rose or caressing the cat has passed,  
when the sunset torching the lawn and the full moon icing it down  
no longer appear, not every man knows what he will discover instead.

When the weight of the past leans against nothing, and the sky  
is no more than remembered light; when the stories of cirrus  
and cumulus draw to a close, and all the birds hang suspended in flight,  
not every man knows what awaits him, or what he shall sing  
when the ship carrying him slips into darkness, there at the end.
outputs.L2:
No man can be certain of the song that will come to him in his final hour,  
As he gazes from the departing vessel toward the shrinking dock.  
He cannot know how it will feel to stand still within the ocean’s thunder,  
Or what desire may remain when returning is no longer possible.  

After the season for trimming roses and stroking the cat has gone,  
After the sun’s blaze across the grass and the moon’s cold silver  
Have vanished from sight, no man can say what will take their place.  

When the burden of memory has nothing left to rest upon,  
When the heavens survive only as a recollection of brightness,  
When the chronicles of high, wispy clouds and billowing ones are finished,  
And every bird hangs unmoving in the air,  
No man knows what awaits him or what words he will sing  
As his vessel glides at last into the dark.
outputs.L3:
The poem reflects on the profound uncertainty surrounding the end of life. It asks what a person might feel, think, or say when faced with their final moment, suggesting that death remains ultimately unknowable. The image of a departing ship symbolizes an irreversible journey away from the familiar world and into death, darkness, and the unknown.

As this journey begins, ordinary pleasures and the beauty of nature gradually recede beyond reach. The sights, sensations, and experiences that once gave life meaning can no longer be held onto. Even memories and stories begin to lose their substance: as the past fades, they become distant and insubstantial, eventually giving way to silence and nothingness.

Ultimately, the poem offers no clear answer about what lies beyond death. Instead, it emphasizes the limits of human knowledge. No one can know with certainty what awaits at the final moment, what words might arise, or whether any hope will remain as life comes to an end.
outputs.L4:
The poem reflects on humanity’s deep uncertainty about death and what, if anything, lies beyond it. A departing ship becomes a powerful symbol of the individual leaving the familiar world behind and moving toward an unknown destination. The surrounding sea reinforces this sense of mystery: vast, shifting, and impossible to fully understand, it represents both the passage toward death and the boundary between life and whatever may follow.

Images of fading nature further emphasize the inevitability of mortality. As light, color, and life gradually disappear, the natural world mirrors the human experience of aging, loss, and decline. The poem’s references to vanished memories also suggest that death involves not only the end of physical existence but the gradual disappearance of personal identity and of the experiences that once gave a life meaning. What was once vivid becomes distant, uncertain, or entirely lost.

Despite these symbolic images, the poem offers no comforting explanation or definite answer. Instead, it acknowledges that no one can know what waits at the end of life or predict how they will respond when the moment arrives. A person may meet death with fear, acceptance, courage, or confusion, but that response cannot be known in advance. By leaving these questions unresolved, the poem presents mortality as one of humanity’s most profound and enduring mysteries.
outputs.L5:
### When No One Is Watching

The world does not stop when no one is watching.

Flowers unfold in empty fields. Stars burn above sleeping towns. A fox slips quietly between the trees, leaving footprints that morning will erase.

We often believe that only visible moments matter—the achievements witnessed, the kindness praised, the courage applauded. Yet character is shaped in private: when recognition is absent, when excuses are easy, and when no one would know the difference.

What we do when others are not watching reveals who we truly are.

counterfactuals.prompt: Give me a lyrical free-verse poem about death, memory, and a ship slipping into darkness, using repeated phrases such as “not every man knows” and “there at the end.”
counterfactuals.output:
**Soundings**

Not every man knows  
the weight of a name  
after the mouth that carried it  
has gone quiet.

Some names become salt,  
some become bells  
heard only at night,  
when the house loosens its boards  
and memory walks barefoot  
from room to room.

There at the end,  
the harbor was a handful of lamps,  
each one trembling  
as if it had something to confess.

The ship moved without farewell—  
black hull, black water,  
a pale wake folding shut behind it  
like a letter no one had finished.

Not every man knows  
how the dead return:

in the scent of rain on rope,  
in a coat left hanging,  
in the sudden warmth  
of an empty chair.

The sea kept no ledger.  
The stars offered no answer.  
Only the engines, far below,  
beat their iron heart  
against the dark.

There at the end,  
we stood along the shore  
with our small, mortal lanterns,  
lifting them higher  
though the ship had passed beyond seeing.

Not every man knows  
when goodbye begins—  
at the final breath,  
or years before,  
when a face first blurs  
at the edges of remembrance.

The ship slipped on,  
past buoy, past bell,  
past the last thin seam  
where water held the sky.

There at the end,  
there was no end—  
only darkness receiving darkness,  
only the long wake vanishing,  
only memory,  
that stubborn light behind us,  
refusing to go out.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
